## Key Findings

### Random vs Importance-Based Pruning

Even the most straightforward methods based on random pruning can yield very encouraging results, though they are generally less sophisticated than importance-based approaches. The random unstructured method does not focus on the importance of features but randomly enforces sparsity, which can sometimes be useful in preventing overfitting or reducing the computational cost.

In contrast, criteria-based approaches rely on a scoring formula to measure the importance of each weight (or filter, neuron, and so on), with commonly used pruning criteria including magnitude, norm, loss change, etc.

### Compound Sparsity Challenges

Recent 2025 research highlights significant challenges when combining multiple compression techniques:

Pruning (which introduces sparsity) and quantization are not orthogonal processes; their associated errors interact in nonlinear and often unpredictable ways, with the cumulative error resulting from quantization followed by pruning typically exceeding the sum of the individual errors and being highly sensitive to the order in which these techniques are applied.

The combination of sparsity and quantization often results in greater accuracy degradation than the sum of their individual effects.

## Overview

MUSTAFAR is a paper titled "Promoting Unstructured Sparsity for KV Cache Pruning in LLM Inference", and it was presented as a NeurIPS 2025 poster.

## Key Findings

MUSTAFAR demonstrates that unstructured sparsity significantly improves KV cache compression for LLMs, enabling sparsity levels up to 70% without compromising accuracy or requiring fine-tuning. 

The work conducts a systematic exploration of pruning strategies and finds per-token magnitude-based pruning as highly effective for both Key and Value caches under unstructured sparsity, surpassing prior structured pruning schemes.

## Technical Approach

The method uses a bitmap-based sparse format and a custom attention kernel capable of compressing and directly computing over compressed caches pruned to arbitrary sparsity patterns, significantly accelerating memory-bound operations in decode computations.

## Performance Results

The custom attention kernel coupled with the bitmap-based format delivers substantial compression of KV cache up to 45% of dense inference and thereby enables longer context length and increased tokens/sec throughput of up to 2.23x compared to dense inference.

The pruning mechanism and sparse attention kernel is available at https://github.com/dhjoo98/mustafar.

## Width vs. Depth Pruning Trade-offs

Width pruning typically achieves better accuracy than depth pruning, though depth pruning often reduces inference latency more at the same number of parameters. The choice between depth pruning, width pruning, or a combination of both should depend on the desired balance between accuracy and latency.

## Joint Optimization Approaches

Recent research explores simultaneous fine-tuning and pruning methods. Researchers have implemented Lagrangian methods to simultaneously fine-tune and prune (SFP) LLMs to a target sparsity, and this approach is directly compatible with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) techniques and can be applied to structures of different granularities.

More specifically, Channel-wise simultaneous fine-tuning and pruning (CSFP) introduces one parameter for each channel in the feed-forward network (FFN) and one for each head in the attention module of a transformer block, while Module-wise simultaneous fine-tuning and pruning (MSFP) introduces one parameter for each FFN layer and one for each attention module in a transformer-based LLM.

## Layer Pruning Research

Recent work also provides insights on layer pruning. Simply pruning the last several layers performs better than many complex pruning metrics. Additionally, LoRA is not the best choice for post-pruning performance recovery, whereas freezing the other layers and fine-tuning only the last few remaining layers and lm_head (partial-layer fine-tuning) can achieve higher accuracy.

## UniComp: A Unified Evaluation Framework

UniComp is a unified evaluation framework for comparing pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation. UniComp evaluates compressed models along three dimensions: performance, reliability, and efficiency, using a diverse set of capability- and safety-oriented benchmarks together with a hardware-aware efficiency analysis.

## Key Findings

Through extensive evaluation of six compression techniques on modern LLMs across more than 40 datasets, the research finds that compression exhibits a consistent knowledge bias, where knowledge-intensive tasks are relatively preserved while reasoning, multilingual, and instruction-following capabilities degrade substantially; quantization provides the best overall trade-off between retained performance and efficiency, whereas distillation yields strong runtime acceleration gains at high computational cost; and task-specific calibration can significantly improve the reasoning ability of pruned models by up to 50%.

## Evaluation Scope

The study conducts extensive experiments on over 40 datasets covering knowledge, reasoning, multilinguality, instruction following, and a wide range of reliability and safety benchmarks, evaluated on modern LLMs including recent chain-of-thought (CoT) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) models.

The paper was recently published on arXiv (arxiv.org/abs/2602.09130) in February 2026 and represents one of the most comprehensive evaluations of LLM compression techniques to date.

I found comprehensive information about SLiM presented at ICML 2025. Here's a summary of the paper:

## Overview

SLiM is a new one-shot compression framework that holistically integrates hardware-friendly quantization, sparsity, and low-rank approximation into a unified process. It is a "one-shot" compression method that reduces a model's size without any expensive retraining by weaving together three contributions: uniform quantization, structured sparsity (pruning), and a low-rank adapter that mathematically corrects the compound errors from the first two steps.

## Technical Approach

The method formulates the quantization process using a probabilistic approach (SLIM-Quant) that enables uniform quantization. Then, it uses an existing one-shot pruning method to apply semi-structured sparsity on top of the quantized weights, and to compensate for the introduced aggregated quantization and sparsity error, it uses a novel saliency function with unique invertible and additive features that enables mathematically computing the value of low-rank adapters.

## Performance Results

SLiM improves model accuracy by up to 5.66% (LLaMA-2-7B) for 2:4 sparsity with 4-bit weight quantization, outperforming prior methods. Models compressed with SLiM achieve up to 4.3× and 3.8× speedup on Nvidia RTX3060 and A100 GPUs, respectively, and achieve up to 0.23× end-to-end memory reduction in comparison to their dense counterparts.

An optional PEFT recipe is also proposed that further improves accuracy by up to 1.66% (LLaMA-2-13B) compared to SLiM without fine-tuning.

The code implementation is available on GitHub at the Paramathic/slim repository.

## Primary Research (May 2026)

The most recent work provides a decision-centric interpretation of performance collapse in layer-pruned LLMs, introducing metrics called Decision Margin and Option Frequency that reveal a stage-structured decision hierarchy with a foundational Silent Phase and a redundant Decisive Phase.

The research shows that Decision Margin undergoes a sharp phase transition, where in early layers it remains consistently negative (the model cannot differentiate correct answers from distractors), but once reaching a critical depth called the Transition Point, it abruptly crosses zero and stabilizes at a positive value, naturally partitioning the model into a Silent Phase and a Decisive Phase.

A key finding is that pruning the Decisive Phase has minimal impact, whereas pruning the Silent Phase triggers immediate performance collapse, indicating that pruning-induced collapse stems from disrupting the Silent Phase, which prevents the critical decision transition from occurring.

## Related Phase Transition Research

Another perspective argues that Large Language Models exhibit Model Phase Transitions where performance collapses beyond critical compression thresholds.

Related work on logical reasoning reveals a similar phenomenon called Logical Phase Transitions, where reasoning performance remains stable within a regime but collapses abruptly beyond a critical logical depth, mirroring physical phase transitions.

These findings represent significant recent advances in understanding why LLMs experience sudden performance drops during layer pruning.

## Phase Transitions in Large Language Model Compression

Large Language Models exhibit Model Phase Transitions: performance collapses beyond critical compression thresholds. A recent perspective published in npj Artificial Intelligence (Nature Portfolio) in February 2026 addresses this phenomenon.

### Key Findings

The research analyzes structural, numerical, and algebraic redundancy across pruning, quantization, and low-rank decomposition techniques, with these sources being orthogonal, enabling a criticality-aware compression framework that achieves near-lossless compression to 10% of the original size.

### Specific Compression Thresholds

Across more than thirty pruning, quantization, and low-rank decomposition techniques, structured pruning fails at 30–45% sparsity, unstructured pruning at 55–65%, low-rank decomposition at 17–30%, and quantization below 3-bit precision.

### Critical Phase Transition Points

Compressed models can suffer from unstable performance, reduced generalization capacity, and, critically, abrupt capability loss when compression exceeds specific thresholds—a critical phenomenon termed the "Phase Transition Point (PTP)," which underscores the non-linear risks inherent in aggressive compression.

By staying within the joint safe region defined by phase-transition points, researchers can raise the prior single-dimension bottleneck, enabling lossless compression to 10% of original model size.

The paper demonstrates that compressing a giant is more effective than training a dwarf for efficient, sustainable AI deployment.

## Overview

PagedEviction is a novel fine-grained, structured KV cache pruning strategy that enhances the memory efficiency of vLLM's PagedAttention. Unlike existing approaches that rely on attention-based token importance or evict tokens across different vLLM pages, PagedEviction introduces an efficient block-wise eviction algorithm tailored for paged memory layouts.

## Technical Approach

PagedEviction integrates seamlessly with PagedAttention without requiring any modifications to its CUDA attention kernels. The method relies on Key and Value tensors to reduce the KV Cache and requires no changes to the CUDA attention kernels. PagedEviction can free entire blocks of KV memory at once, avoiding the fragmentation or overhead that token-level evictions might introduce.

## Key Contributions

PagedEviction operates in both prefill and decode phases. During prefill, tokens are evicted based on per-token importance before block partitioning. During decode, an entire block is evicted only after the most recent block becomes full, reducing fragmentation and per-step eviction overhead.

## Performance Results

On LongBench datasets, PagedEviction consistently outperforms other attention-free baselines. For example, on GovReport with LLaMA-3.2-1B, it achieves a ROUGE score of 24.5 at a 1024-token budget, outperforming StreamingLLM (21.0) and KeyDiff (21.2) by 15–20%. At a cache budget of 1024, PagedEviction achieves up to 3020 tokens/sec on LLaMA-1B, a 37% improvement over Full Cache (2200 tokens/sec), and a 39% improvement over Inverse Key L2-Norm (2170 tokens/sec).

## "Doing More With Less: Revisiting the Effectiveness of LLM Pruning for Test-Time Scaling"

Unstructured pruning augments test-time scaling (TTS) performance compared to structured pruning, and at times can even outperform unpruned full-weight LLMs across four reasoning benchmarks on two reasoning LLMs: s1.1-7B and Qwen3-8B.

### Key Results:

The performance of unstructured pruned models matches that of the unpruned baseline for s1.1-7B, while for Qwen3-8B, they consistently exceed it.

Experiments across all four reasoning datasets and both LLMs demonstrate a consistent conclusion: unstructured pruning not only outperforms structured pruning, but also retains or, on most occasions, outperforms the performance of the unpruned LLMs.

### Broader Implications:

These findings challenge the conventional notion that pruning always reduces TTS performance and suggest that carefully undertaken pruning can improve TTS effectiveness even further.

The research was published in April 2026 on arXiv and investigates the intersection of LLM pruning and test-time scaling, challenging prior assumptions that pruning necessarily degrades reasoning capabilities.

I found detailed information about "The Sparse Frontier" paper. Here's a summary of the search results:

## Overview

"The Sparse Frontier: Sparse Attention Trade-offs in Transformer LLMs" addresses sparse attention as a promising strategy to extend long-context capabilities in Transformer LLMs, yet its efficiency-accuracy trade-offs remain unclear due to the lack of comprehensive evaluation.

## Research Scope

The paper presents the largest-scale empirical analysis to date of training-free sparse attention, evaluating six methods across multiple model families and sizes, sequences up to 128K tokens, and sparsity levels up to 0.95 (i.e., 1/20 attention budget) on nine diverse tasks.

## Key Findings

The research reveals several important insights:

1. **Model Scale Advantages**: An isoFLOPS analysis reveals that for very long sequences, larger and highly sparse models are preferable to smaller and dense ones.

2. **Decoding vs. Prefilling**: The level of sparsity attainable while statistically guaranteeing accuracy preservation is higher during decoding than prefilling, and correlates with model size in the former.

3. **No Universal Solution**: There is no clear strategy that performs best across tasks and phases, with different units of sparsification or budget adaptivity needed for different scenarios. Even moderate sparsity levels often result in significant performance degradation on at least one task, highlighting that sparse attention is not a universal solution.

4. **Scaling Laws**: The paper introduces and validates novel scaling laws specifically tailored for sparse attention, providing evidence that their findings are likely to hold true beyond their range of experiments.

## Overall Conclusion

The research demonstrates that sparse attention is a key tool to enhance the capabilities of Transformer LLMs for processing longer sequences, but requires careful evaluation of trade-offs for performance-sensitive applications.

The paper was initially posted on April 24, 2025, with an updated version on January 27, 2026.

## GRASPrune Overview

GRASPrune is a structured pruning framework applied after pretraining that jointly prunes FFN channels and KV head groups under a single global budget.

## Key Technical Approach

Instead of learning importance scores without constraints and applying the budget only after training, GRASPrune learns lightweight gate scores with a projected straight-through estimator that enforces a hard mask satisfying the budget at every step while keeping the backbone weights frozen. After the mask is fixed, scaling factors on the retained units are calibrated to mitigate scale mismatch caused by pruning, and these factors are folded into the pruned weights to obtain a smaller dense checkpoint with no extra parameters at inference.

## Performance Results

Experiments on LLaMA-style models show that the method better preserves language-modeling performance than existing structured pruning baselines across a wide range of parameter ratios, with especially large gains in high-compression regimes. For example, on LLaMA-2-7B, GRASPrune removes 50% of parameters and achieves 12.18 perplexity on WikiText-2.

## Publication Status

GRASPrune has been accepted as an ACL 2026 Main conference paper on global gating for budgeted structured pruning of LLMs. The implementation currently supports LLaMA-style and Qwen-style models.
